prompt: Which of these does the course leave to the interpreter, with no engine function doing it?
options: Returning the exact plane-wave reflection coefficient at each angle for the zone top, which zoeppritzRpp computes.
Fitting measured Vs on Vp by least squares and giving the prediction interval, which fitVsRegression and predictVs return.
Deciding whether the QI study should go ahead; a person writes that verdict from the spectra, trends, moduli and reflection coefficients.
Averaging the power of many traces into one spectrum and taking the root, which averageSpectrum does on the stated traces.
explanation: The engines return spectra, trends, moduli and reflection coefficients, and the verdict is written by the interpreter from those numbers. zoeppritzRpp, fitVsRegression with predictVs, and averageSpectrum are all engine functions the course calls, the last one on the 120 spread traces.

prompt: The Ekene fluids are computed at 180 degF. Where does that temperature come from when an engine runs?
options: From the caller, as a stated input; the engines hold no Ekene figure.
From a table of Ekene conditions held inside fluids.js, which brine falls back on whenever the caller passes no temperature.
From the well header file and the clock, which the engine reads at run time so the conditions match the date of the logs.
From a random draw around 180 degF made on each call.
explanation: Every temperature, pressure, salinity and oil gravity is an input the caller states, and the course states 180 degF, 3200 psia, salinity 0.035000 and 32 API with the kit. No engine reads a file, a clock or a random number of its own, and none keeps an Ekene table.

prompt: What is the Ekene field that the teaching pack is cut from?
options: A producing field in the Niger Delta whose well, company and survey names were changed before the pack was cut.
A published benchmark field from Batzle and Wang (1992), reprinted with its logs.
Figures measured in the QI with Petrolord videos, cut to four wells.
A synthetic demonstration field: one earth model, with every log and trace generated by a stated script.
explanation: The Ekene field is the Petrolord demonstration field, generated from one earth model by a stated script so every answer can be checked against the model. No real well, company or survey appears. Batzle and Wang (1992) is the reference for brine and live oil properties, and the pack is cut from release ekene-demo-v3 by the course's cut script.

prompt: At Ekene-2 the top of the Ekene Sand is at 5134.514436 ft and the oil-water contact at 5118.110236 ft. What does the oil leg selection return there?
options: 65 samples, the same as Ekene-1, because the contact sits at one depth in every well and so cuts every sand alike.
No samples: the oil leg is 0 and the water leg 187.
114 samples, since above the contact the selection keeps going up into the Ogbia Shale until it finds net sand.
130 samples, the cap rock count, which the selection reads as the oil leg when the whole sand lies below the contact.
explanation: A well whose top of the Ekene Sand lies below the oil-water contact has no oil leg by the rule, and the course tables Ekene-2 at net sand 187, oil leg 0, water leg 187. 65 is Ekene-1's oil leg, 114 is Ekene-3's, and 130 is the cap rock at every pack well.

prompt: In the course's vocabulary, a distance from the wet trend is signed. Which side is negative?
options: The brine side, so a wet sand reads negative and a hydrocarbon sand positive.
The hydrocarbon side.
Neither: a perpendicular distance is a magnitude, so the course prints it without a sign.
The hydrocarbon side when read from the published line, and the brine side from the fitted line.
explanation: The distance is the signed perpendicular distance of an (A, B) point from a stated line, and negative is the hydrocarbon side whichever line is stated. At Ekene-1 the top reads -0.072091 in situ against -0.004519 with brine, so the oil moves it further to the negative side.

prompt: A learner types an interval level of 1.2 into predictVs in the feasibility explorer. What does the panel show?
options: A prediction at the nearest valid level, 0.900000, with a warning line saying the stated level was replaced.
A prediction with NaN in its low and high fields.
The engine's own words: "The sample interval must be positive.", since the level is read as an interval.
The engine's own words: "The interval level must be between 0 and 1."
explanation: When an engine cannot answer it throws, and the panel prints its message unchanged; predictVs at a level of 1.2 gives "The interval level must be between 0 and 1." Nothing is replaced, NaN fields belong to elasticPoint, which does not throw, and the sample interval message is amplitudeSpectrum's refusal of a 0 ms interval.

prompt: Which samples does the course's cap rock selection take at Ekene-1?
options: The 65 ft of log above the top of the Ekene Sand, 130 samples.
The whole Ogbia Shale, from its top down to the sand.
The oil leg, 65 samples of net sand below the top.
Every sample inside the Ekene Sand with Vsh above 0.350000, the shale the net sand cut-off leaves out.
explanation: The cap rock is the 65 ft of log above the top of the Ekene Sand, 130 samples at every pack well, read as one layer by its means. The net sand above the contact is the oil leg, 65 samples at Ekene-1, and the Ekene-1 logs start at 4931.500000 ft, far below the top of the Ogbia Shale at 4232.283465 ft.

prompt: How does the course treat the two gassmann.js messages that are missing from its table of refusals?
options: It quotes both in full beside the other 21 refusals, because every engine message is printed between quotation marks.
It leaves them out because substituteVels never throws, and reports a bad porosity as a result with NaN fields.
It names each by what it refuses and does not quote it, because each carries a punctuation mark the course does not print.
It counts them among the 21 refusals across 14 functions, and prints them under elasticPoint, which covers the same inputs.
explanation: Two more messages exist in gassmann.js, an implied saturated modulus that is not positive and an inverse Gassmann dry modulus that is not positive; the course names them and does not print them. substituteVels does throw, for example "Porosity must be in (0, 1)." at a porosity of 0, and the 21 refusals are the tabled ones.

prompt: The Ekene-1 oil-leg AI (acoustic impedance) of the means is 6639018.603084 kg/(m2 s). A second source writes the same rock as 6639.018603. Which unit is that source using?
options: Units of 10^6 kg/(m2 s), the form a crossplot axis uses to keep impedance in single figures.
SI, the shear impedance Vs x density.
kg/(m2 s) with the density taken from the oil leg's pore fluid in place of the bulk log density.
(m/s)(g/cc), that is AI divided by 1000.
explanation: The same AI is 6639018.603084 in kg/(m2 s), 6.639019 in units of 10^6 kg/(m2 s) and 6639.018603 in (m/s)(g/cc). The oil-leg SI is 3795337.170439 kg/(m2 s), and AI is Vp times the bulk density of the leg, 2316.676923 kg/m3.

prompt: At Ekene-1 the top of the Ekene Sand reads OWT 644.398189 ms, linear between two checkshots. What time should a learner look for on the seismic?
options: 644.398189 ms, since the seismic and the checkshot both record one-way time from the reference.
585.055000 ms, the one-way time of the checkshot at 4687.500000 ft above the top.
644.438000 ms, the time of the checkshot at 5079.002625 ft, the level nearest the top.
explanation: Seismic time is two-way time and a checkshot records one-way time, so the top at OWT 644.398189 ms is at TWT 1288.796378 ms. 585.055000 and 644.438000 ms are the one-way times of the bracketing checkshots, and both are one-way.

prompt: On the kit's SEG normal polarity seismic, how does the top of the Ekene Sand appear at Ekene-1?
options: As a peak, a positive number, because AI (acoustic impedance) increases downwards from the Ogbia Shale into the harder sand.
As a trough, since SEG normal polarity writes an increase in impedance downwards as a negative number.
As a trough, because oil softens the sand at Ekene-1 below the AI (acoustic impedance) of the shale above it.
As a peak only where the sand is wet; at Ekene-1 the oil leg's lower AI (acoustic impedance) makes it a trough.
explanation: On SEG normal polarity an increase in acoustic impedance downwards is a peak, a positive number. At Ekene-1 the cap rock's mean AI is 4697628.723902 kg/(m2 s) and the oil leg's 6639018.603084, so even with oil the sand is harder and its top is a peak.

prompt: The kit writes the top of the Ekene Sand at Ekene-1 as 1548.000000 m. What does the course print for it?
options: 1548.000000 ft, the kit's depth kept as written.
5118.110236 ft, the kit's 1560.000000 m converted.
5078.740157 ft, converted from the kit's metres by feet = metres / 0.3048.
4232.283465 ft, the top of the Ogbia Shale.
explanation: Depths are feet throughout, feet = metres / 0.3048, and the top at Ekene-1 is 5078.740157 ft (1548.000000 m in the kit). 5118.110236 ft is the oil-water contact (1560.000000 m) and 4232.283465 ft is the top of the Ogbia Shale.

prompt: Which of these could be a graded capstone figure at the Associate tier?
options: An engine's return value on a held-out synthetic case that the learner pastes into the feasibility explorer.
The Ekene median signal to noise of 361.155122, read from the 800 to 1600 ms window as the verdict quotes it.
The usability grade of Ekene-9, missing, since a grade is a return value of QI Studio's own function on the headers.
A figure spoken in a QI with Petrolord video, since the videos run the same engines on the Ekene field.
explanation: Every graded field is an engine return value on a held-out synthetic case supplied as a case file, and the case is never Ekene. No Ekene figure, no usability grade and no figure in the videos is graded; the videos speak the Ekene answers aloud, which is why Ekene is never graded.

prompt: Which reference does the course name for signal to noise from trace coherency?
options: Castagna, Swan and Foster (1998), whose background trend the course also uses to read noise off a crossplot.
Goodway, Chen and Downton (1997), the source of the elastic set's lambda-rho and mu-rho.
Rutherford and Williams (1989), with class IV, whose classes sort a trace by its signal.
Hatton, Worthington and Makin (1986).
explanation: Signal to noise from coherency is Hatton, Worthington and Makin (1986), in seismicQc.js. Castagna, Swan and Foster (1998) is the wet background trend, Goodway, Chen and Downton (1997) is lambda-rho and mu-rho, and Rutherford and Williams (1989) is the AVO classes.

prompt: How does the course use the published references behind its engines?
options: It quotes each paper's own explanation with credit, since a method is best taught in its authors' words.
It names each by its authors and year and teaches it by concept and equation in its own words, quoting none of their prose.
It prints the engines' source comments as its teaching text, since they restate each paper exactly.
It re-derives every method in full, Batzle-Wang, Gassmann and Shuey among them, in each lesson that uses one.
explanation: Every method is named with its authors and year and the course quotes none of their prose, teaching each by concept and equation. The engines' source comments are provenance, and the Rock Physics course teaches Batzle-Wang, Gassmann and Shuey in full while this course recaps each in one lesson.
